targeting_context.jd_text:
Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships
San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY | Seattle, WA

About Anthropic

Anthropic's mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

As the Manager of the Partnerships Applied AI Solutions Architect team, you will drive adoption of frontier AI by enabling deployment of Anthropic's products (Claude for Enterprise, Claude Code, API) through our Global and Regional System Integrators, cloud partners (AWS, GCP, Azure), and strategic technology partners.

You will build and lead a team of Partner Solutions Architects, establish processes and best practices for partner-led pre-sales engagements, and represent Anthropic as the technical lead on its most important partnerships. In collaboration with Sales, Partnerships, Product, and Engineering, you will help partners incorporate leading-edge AI into their practices, accelerate indirect revenue, and execute long-term GTM strategy while maintaining our best-in-class safety standards.

Responsibilities

    Team Leadership & Development: Hire, manage, and mentor a team of Partner Solutions Architects. Set goals, run reviews, and coach each team member toward high productivity and career growth.
    Strategic Technical Partnership: Act as the senior technical thought partner to Anthropic's GTM partnerships team. Co-build partner strategy with aligned GTM leadership, drive key programs, and align cross-functional stakeholders (Sales, Product, Engineering) behind partner outcomes.
    Partner Enablement & Ecosystem: Embed your team with GSI and cloud partner technical teams to enable their AI practices, troubleshoot, and evangelize Anthropic in their developer communities. Represent Anthropic at partner events (GSI workshops, AWS/GCP summits, hackathons) and contribute technical content and thought leadership.
    Joint Solution Development: Lead partners in identifying high-value, industry-specific GenAI applications. Develop joint solutions and codify reference architectures and best practices to accelerate time to deployment.
    Customer Deal Support: Own the technical portion of partner-led pre-sales engagements. Intervene directly on strategic deals where partners are the primary delivery vehicle, providing deep solution architecture guidance.
    Product Feedback: Gather and validate feedback on Anthropic's products from partner deployments and deliver it to Product and Engineering to inform roadmap and partner strategy.

You may be a good fit if you have

    7+ years in technical customer-facing or partner-facing roles (Solutions Architect, Sales Engineer, Partner SE, TAM).
    3+ years managing pre-sales or partner-facing technical teams; comfortable building foundational teams in ambiguous, fast-moving environments.
    Track record building and scaling partnerships with GSIs (e.g., Accenture, Deloitte, TCS, Infosys) and/or cloud providers (AWS, GCP, Azure).
    Deep understanding of partner-led selling and delivery: indirect revenue models, enablement at scale, and joint GTM motions.
    Technical depth in enterprise AI deployments: LLM architecture, prompt engineering, evaluation, API integrations, and production use cases.
    Exceptional communication and executive presence; able to build trusted relationships with C-suite, partner leadership, and engineering teams alike.
    A love of teaching and mentoring, and a passion for advancing safe, beneficial AI.

Strong candidates may also have

    5+ years leading partner-facing SA teams through hypergrowth, including developing both senior and junior talent.
    Direct experience helping GSIs or consultancies build their AI/ML practice - enablement programs, certification paths, joint solution development.

Compensation

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role's On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary: $315,000 - $380,000 USD

# Anthropic - Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships briefing packet
| Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships | $315,000–$380,000 USD | Reports to Partnerships (partner-led applied AI architecture) |

## JD Complement
This position connects Anthropic’s safety-oriented product identity with the implementation realities of large enterprises. External firms will need to turn model capability into durable operating practices, trusted workflows, and
outcomes customers can measure.

The core tension is expansion without drift. Anthropic can extend reach through external technical capacity, but partner work must remain consistent with the company’s standards for reliability, security, user trust, and responsible use.

## Company DNA & Operating Model
Anthropic is a public benefit corporation focused on AI research, product development, and practical enterprise use. Its identity is closely tied to building AI systems that are dependable, understandable, and controllable.

The company serves both business users and technical builders through Claude offerings. That creates an adoption model where value is realized not simply through access to a model, but through integration into real work, software,
governance processes, and organizational habits.

Enterprise success likely depends on making a rapidly evolving product usable in complex environments with established security, identity, compliance, procurement, and change-management requirements. The most useful field patterns will
be those that balance speed with repeatability.

## Company Strategy & Operating Pressure
Anthropic’s enterprise proposition combines advanced AI capability with an emphasis on safety, accuracy, and security. This can resonate with organizations that need confidence in how AI is introduced, monitored, and expanded, while also
creating a higher bar for implementation quality.

Claude addresses a broad set of knowledge-work and development use cases. The commercial challenge is connecting executive priorities, business-team adoption, developer workflows, administrative controls, and technical integration into
a coherent customer journey.

Public deployment materials indicate that successful rollout extends beyond configuration. It includes organizational launch, user adoption, and continuous improvement. As a result, technical validation alone is unlikely to determine
long-term account value; sustained usage and operating fit matter as much as an initial demonstration.

A likely internal pressure point is deciding what should be globally standardized versus adapted for a particular sector, customer environment, cloud stack, or delivery organization. Clear boundaries can reduce one-off work while
preserving flexibility where it matters.

## Leadership & Stakeholder Map
The relevant stakeholder map is functional and outcome-oriented:

- Product and engineering will benefit from field signals that distinguish recurring product needs from customer-specific delivery requests.

## AI, Data, Platform, Architecture Signals
Anthropic presents Claude as an assistant intended to be safe, accurate, and secure. Its enterprise materials emphasize controls and support for both organizational users and developers.

The relevant architecture conversation therefore extends beyond prompts or model selection. It includes workflow design, application integration, access management, data handling, evaluation approaches, human oversight, and operational
governance.

Because Claude is positioned for analysis, coding, and complex problem solving, adoption will be highly dependent on context. Strong implementation patterns should connect AI capability to a customer’s actual processes, software
environment, user groups, and risk posture.

Anthropic’s research-and-safety identity has commercial implications. In enterprise settings, architecture quality is inseparable from confidence: customers need to understand how the technology fits their controls and how it can be
expanded responsibly.

## Partnership / Ecosystem Motion
Anthropic publicly describes an ecosystem that includes cloud, technology, and services organizations. This suggests that external routes to market and delivery capacity are important components of enterprise scale.

Each partner type can contribute differently. Cloud firms may support infrastructure alignment and procurement paths; technology firms may embed or integrate Claude into complementary products; service providers may help customers redesign
work, implement solutions, and build internal capability.

Anthropic and Accenture publicly frame their relationship around enterprise AI deployment, productivity, value creation, and new-product creation. This points to an ecosystem where joint customer work and reusable solution patterns can
matter more than simple referrals.

The operating test is likely whether partners can deliver consistently without requiring extensive internal intervention. Useful mechanisms may include architecture guidance, enablement paths, reusable assets, qualification standards,
feedback channels, and effective escalation routes.

## Recent Events & Urgency
Current public materials emphasize enterprise adoption, administrator guidance, business and developer use cases, and an ecosystem of cloud, technology, and services firms. Together, these signals suggest a shift from availability of
frontier models toward disciplined operational use in large organizations.

The urgency is not just ecosystem expansion. It is establishing repeatable partner-supported delivery before customer expectations, implementation variation, and product velocity make field quality harder to manage.

Enterprise AI competition increasingly turns on moving customers from experimentation into secure, governed, high-value usage. Anthropic’s positioning can be differentiated in that transition if external delivery organizations can
translate it into credible technical and organizational outcomes.

## apps_rg Positioning Themes (targeting only, not proof)
- Scaling enterprise AI adoption through external technical ecosystems rather than through standalone alliance management.
- Leading technical teams that operate across cloud, services, and software-partner environments.
- Creating reusable production patterns for AI-enabled workflows, integrations, controls, and evaluation.
- Enabling consultancies and systems integrators to deliver high-quality customer outcomes independently.
- Bridging solution architecture with adoption planning, organizational readiness, and user value realization.
- Applying security, governance, and responsible-use considerations to enterprise AI implementation.
- Building structured field-to-product feedback from real customer and partner deployment experience.
- Raising technical consistency across complex commercial cycles without over-centralizing delivery.
- Working effectively across revenue, partnerships, product, engineering, and customer-facing teams.
- Translating frontier-model capabilities into industry- and workflow-specific business value.

## apps_lic Outreach Angles (targeting only, not proof)
- Anthropic’s ecosystem spans cloud, technology, and service providers, making technical partner execution consequential to enterprise growth.
- Its enterprise adoption materials acknowledge that configuration is only one part of a successful customer rollout.
- The role is likely central to converting partner expertise into repeatable customer delivery capacity.
- Anthropic’s emphasis on safety, reliability, and security increases the value of disciplined architecture in the field.
- The compelling leadership problem is expanding joint customer outcomes while preserving a coherent implementation experience.

## Do Not Use As Proof
The JD and this briefing are targeting inputs only. Candidate claims, achievements, scope, leadership experience, technical depth, and partnership outcomes must come from the governed resume/proof graph.

rubric:
Rubric dimensions (graph-only C0.3 augmented skills graph authority, non-SRFS lane):
1. factual_support: claims supported by allowed_fact_packet and candidate claim_ledger source_fact_ids only.
   **For rows carrying `display_override_text`, the authorized substrate is the UNION of `claim_text` +
   `display_override_text`. Phrases from `display_override_text` are deterministically authorized — do NOT
   flag them as unsupported, inferential, or out-of-scope extensions; the generator was X2-required to emit
   them verbatim. When `graph_proof_refs.claim_support_graph_refs` is non-empty, also authorize prose that
   demonstrates those skill nodes; `graph_proof_refs.source_resume_files` is authoritative provenance.
   Cite a `factual_support` failure only when prose deviates from the full authorized union (claim +
   override + graph skill refs).**
2. executive_signal: SVP-level platform/governance/partner-motion synthesis, not bullet stacks.
3. resume_voice: credible executive prose; no recruiter filler, meta narration, or generic AI-company prose, and nothing that would fail a Head of Talent Acquisition screen.
4. ats_alignment_without_keyword_stuffing: JD shapes emphasis only; no JD-as-proof. When allowed facts
   lack EA/interop/federated proof IDs, penalize only if prose invents those themes or ignores documented
   gap_notes — not for absence alone when generation_law_digest requires gap_notes. Reward company-DNA specificity when the
   packet supports partner ecosystem, adoption motion, commercial fit, or a clean Head of Talent Acquisition screen.
5. anti_overfit: no unsupported metrics/credentials; no target company as candidate experience; no repeated metric inventory
   or company-name mirroring; no AI-authenticity dead giveaways such as em dashes, buzzword soup, or template phrasing.
   **`display_override_text` content is NOT an unsupported credential/metric — it is X2-authorized
   substrate. Do not cite override phrases (e.g. "FSA-chartered", "informing data governance and AI
   strategy at scale") as anti_overfit violations.**
6. synthesis_quality: **exactly six** integrated sentences (X2 band); reward connective SVP IT strategy emphasis when
   ledger-backed; penalize thin recap S6, repeated metric surfaces, and bullet-stacked prose. **Do not** soft-penalize
   credential/metric inventory, unused_fact_ids weave targets, or mechanism dumps when the mapped deterministic gate shows `"pass": true`.
   Keep the cadence human enough to pass a Head of Talent Acquisition screen without machine-generated tells.
7. evidence_utilization: when `x2_exec_summary_evidence_utilization` is `"pass": true`, unused_fact_ids are optional weave
   targets — not proof gaps. Penalize under-use only when that gate is `"pass": false` or synthesis is decisively thin;
   reward distinct evidence themes instead of the same metric repeated in multiple sentences.
8. deterministic_alignment: **only** penalize gates that show `"pass": false` in deterministic_gate_summary. Never cite
   retired five-part/S1–S5 arc mandates when gates passed.

Residual quality (always in scope — not closed by X2 alone):
- executive clarity, narrative coherence, commercial fit, usefulness, unsupported phrasing outside ledger scope.

Decisive failure triggers (must align with deterministic_gate_summary failures when cited):
- unsupported business metric or credential (when x2 gates failed or decisive unsupported claim)
- JD or briefing used as proof
- first-person narrative
- obvious rewrite recommendation that invents new claims
